title: Astrid and the Vector
premise: Ines Halloran, an insurance investigator who ferries claims between two fleets that severed contact decades ago, discovers a ship on her manifest that never flew—carrying the name Astrid Voss, her own mother's alias. The 'ship' is a forged peace treaty disguised as cargo paperwork, and someone is using Ines's invisible route to keep the lie alive that both fleets still honor it. As she traces the forgery through smugglers, defectors, and her mother's old crew, Ines must choose between exposing the fraud (which would reignite war) or becoming its new keeper. She ends by burning her investigator's credentials and taking over the route herself, adopting Astrid's name as her own, with the found family of the route's misfit couriers standing watch beside her.
about_author: Rosalind Oyelaran is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent six years routing documents between ports that officially had no trade relations. She writes science fiction about bureaucracy as love language from a houseboat in Lagos.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Ines Halloran's POV. Processing routine claims between the Meridian and Halcyon fleets, Ines finds a vessel on her manifest—the Astrid Voss—with no flight history, no registry, and her mother's name. Her supervisor dismisses it; her instinct doesn't. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm, the first crack in a life built on staying unnoticed.

chapters.title: Paper Wars
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with interludes from courier Teodor Okonkwo. Following the forgery's paper trail, Ines meets the route's hidden community—smugglers and defectors who've kept unofficial peace for years—and learns the treaty is fiction they all maintain. Teodor warns her someone else is hunting the file. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging; she stops being alone.

chapters.title: Astrid
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The hunter—a Halcyon hardliner named Captain Reye—captures Teodor and offers Ines a trade: the file for his life. Digging into her mother's past, Ines realizes Astrid Voss wrote the original fake treaty to prevent a war, then vanished into it. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve; duty and love become the same choice.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climaxing in a standoff at the neutral relay station. Ines trades herself for Teodor, then confronts Reye with proof that exposing the lie kills more than it avenges—including his own family on the route's rolls. Reye stands down; the courier network formalizes around her. Emotional beat: Ines signs her mother's name as her own, invisible no longer, home found.
